headline: Semis Shine, Breadth Limps Into Monday's Open
body_html:
Futures are digesting a lopsided Friday session as traders step into a week front-loaded with geopolitical catalysts. The most recent completed session — Friday, September 18 — saw declining issues outpace advancers by a wide margin, 340 down against 204 up across a 545-name universe, with only two of eight tracked sectors finishing in positive territory. Semiconductors led the tape with a sector gain of 2.47%, buoyed by outsized moves in memory and equipment names, while Homebuilders sank 1.62% and Software slid 1.03%.

Monday's pre-market tone will be shaped heavily by developments in the Middle East. Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains thin as the regional conflict drags on, Houthi strikes on Saudi targets have rattled Gulf equity markets, and oil is pulling back on nascent hopes for diplomacy between Tehran and Washington. Any shift in that diplomatic read could reprice energy futures quickly at the open.

On the macro-diplomatic front, the United Nations General Assembly convenes this week, with a packed meeting schedule expected from Washington. A high-profile Xi-Trump summit, arriving against the backdrop of strong Chinese trade data, adds another variable for multinationals. Investors should watch whether that constructive trade signal sustains or fades as formal talks begin.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Equipment Names Drove Friday's Only Sector Win
briefs.body: Lam Research surged 6.98% and Applied Materials added 6.51% on Friday, anchoring a 2.47% sector-wide advance for semiconductors — the lone bright spot in an otherwise defensive session. Sandisk topped the leaderboard with an 11% jump, while MaxLinear rose more than 8%, reflecting renewed appetite for memory and chip-supply-chain exposure.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Traffic Thin as Regional Tensions Hold Shipping on Edge
briefs.body: Tanker passage through the Strait of Hormuz has slowed to a trickle amid the ongoing Middle East conflict, raising supply-chain vigilance for energy traders heading into the week. With Houthi forces claiming strikes on Riyadh-area targets, Gulf equity markets fell sharply over the weekend, adding a risk-off undercurrent to Monday's open.

briefs.headline: Oil Retreats on Diplomatic Overtures Toward Iran
briefs.body: Crude prices slid heading into the new week as markets priced in a modest probability of dialogue between Tehran and Washington. The move comes even as Iran and the United States continued to exchange threats following an escalation in Houthi activity, leaving the net directional call on oil highly sensitive to any fresh headline.

briefs.headline: Xi Arrives at Trump Summit With Trade Numbers Backing His Hand
briefs.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping enters a high-profile meeting with President Trump with the country's trade engine running at a notable pace, according to Reuters. The timing — coinciding with the UN General Assembly — elevates the encounter's market significance, particularly for sectors with heavy supply-chain exposure to China.

briefs.headline: France Enters Diplomatic Fray After Iran Shutters Language Centre
briefs.body: Tehran closed a French cultural and language facility, accusing it of operating outside legal bounds, prompting a formal warning of retaliation from Paris. The move adds a European dimension to the already complex Iran standoff and could complicate any multilateral diplomatic effort on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly this week.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders and Materials Shares Bore the Brunt of Friday's Selling
briefs.body: Homebuilders dropped 1.62% on Friday — the steepest sectoral decline of the session — while Materials fell 1.05%, with metallurgical coal name Alpha Metallurgical Resources sliding nearly 5.7% and steelmaker Nucor shedding more than 6%. The broad weakness in rate-sensitive and commodity-linked names kept overall market breadth firmly negative heading into the weekend.
